title: Lab Safety & Equipment Scavenger Hunt
subtitle: 8 Stations · Get Students Moving · Full Answer Key with Explanations

items: Print the station cards (pages 2–3) and cut them apart.
Hang the cards around the room — walls, benches, windows.
Print one Student Answer Sheet per student (page 4).
Students work in pairs, rotate through stations, and record answers.
Collect answer sheets and review with the Answer Key (last page).

items.title: Safety Symbols
items.clue: This yellow triangle shows a hand being eaten away.
items.task: Name the hazard and give one rule for working with it.
items.explain: The corrosion symbol warns of chemicals that burn skin, eyes, and materials. Rule: wear gloves and goggles, handle with care.

items.title: Eyewash Station
items.clue: It is the first stop if chemicals get in your eyes.
items.task: How long should you rinse? What should you do first?
items.answer: Rinse 15 minutes; tell the teacher first
items.explain: Alert the teacher, then flush both eyes at the eyewash for at least 15 minutes, holding eyelids open.

items.title: Lab Attire
items.clue: Not stylish, but they protect your eyes and your feet.
items.task: Name the two required items of lab attire and explain why.
items.explain: Goggles protect eyes from splashes; closed-toe shoes protect feet from spills and broken glass.

items.title: Heating Safely
items.clue: You should never leave this burning unattended.
items.task: Give two rules for using a Bunsen burner safely.
items.answer: Never leave unattended; tie back hair; keep flammables away; light with a striker
items.explain: Open flames demand attention: secure hair/clothes, keep paper away, use a striker, and never walk away.

items.title: Chemical Handling
items.clue: The label is your best friend — read it twice.
items.task: Why must you read the label before using any chemical?
items.answer: To know hazards, handling, and first aid
items.explain: Labels carry GHS pictograms, hazard statements, and handling instructions — read before every use.

items.title: Acid Dilution
items.clue: Do as you oughter: add this to water, not the other way.
items.task: State the correct way to dilute concentrated acid and why.
items.answer: Add acid to water slowly, stirring
items.explain: Dilution is exothermic; adding acid to water slowly lets heat dissipate safely instead of splashing.

items.title: Glassware
items.clue: Measures volume, but it is NOT for heating.
items.task: Which glassware should you use to measure liquids, and which for heating?
items.answer: Graduated cylinder for measuring; borosilicate beaker for heating
items.explain: Graduated cylinders measure precisely but crack when heated; use borosilicate (Pyrex) glassware for heating.

items.title: Emergencies
items.clue: If this happens, tell the teacher and never touch it with bare hands.
items.task: What is the correct response to a broken beaker?
items.answer: Tell the teacher; sweep carefully into glass container
items.explain: Never pick up broken glass bare-handed — sweep it up and place it in the glass disposal container, then inform the teacher.
